reason: Inermis/inerme means unarmed, i.e. without spines, thorns or prickles. PATO:0001365 spiny covers spines, thorns or similar projections, and 'aculeate' was already mapped to it.
This is a spelling variant of an existing FLOPO value class.

label: glandular-dentate
definition: A dentated quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's margin bearing teeth that are tipped with glands.
reason: This is not a continuum between dentate and glandular: it says the teeth carry glands. It follows the earlier gland classes (stipitate-glandular, glandular-pubescent, gland-dotted).

target: continuum of two values (docs/annotation-context-patterns.md §2; chain_from_phrase): prolate (ellipsoid) – cylindrical (PATO_0001873)
reason: This is a hyphenated compound of two shapes, read as a continuum between them. The playbook reads 'ellipsoid' as prolate.
This is a fusion with a different named part: adnate, with the petiole as the other part of the relation.

label: intrapetiolar
definition: A positional quality inhering in a stipule by virtue of its being placed in the leaf axil, between the petiole and the stem, often united with the other stipule of the leaf.
reason: This is a standard stipule position with no term. FLOPO axillary is about parts arising in an axil and does not cover stipule position. It is botany-specific, beside the position classes added in the previous review.
Same as the earlier rule for crateriform, which was mapped to PATO:0040009 bowl shaped.

target: new: two values joined without a connector (both hold; not a continuum): lanceolate (PATO_0001877) on the part + acute (FLOPO:0991095) on its apex (FLOPO_0985023)
reason: This is a lanceolate part with an acute tip, not a shape between lanceolate and acute. Reading it as a continuum would be wrong.
'En gouttière' means channelled lengthwise, i.e. canaliculate. That was mapped to grooved in the previous review.

label: marginate
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having a distinct border that differs from the rest of the bearer in colour, texture or thickness.
reason: Marginate is a standard glossary term with no PATO or FLOPO class. 'Narrowly' is the width of the border and goes in as a modifier. On petioles it may mean narrowly winged (PATO_0104354), so check those cases.
This names a plant group (Cyperaceae), not a quality. 'Perennial' in the same phrase is annotated on its own.
This states that the lateral veins are absent, the same way 'veinless' became vascular bundle absent. For lemmas, PO_0020140 fits less well, so it may need vascular bundle with a lateral position.
This says the parts vary, but not how. It has no content without the values it summarizes.
This gives where the widest point is, not one shape: obovate, oblanceolate and spatulate are all broadest above the middle. It usually appears in alternatives ('above or near the middle').

target: continuum of two values (docs/annotation-context-patterns.md §2; chain_from_phrase): pubescent hair (PATO_0001320) – villous (FLOPO:0991051)
reason: This is a hyphenated compound of two hair types, an intermediate between them.

target: continuum of two values (docs/annotation-context-patterns.md §2; chain_from_phrase): ovate (FLOPO:0991024) – orbicular (PATO_0001934)
reason: This is a hyphenated compound of two plane shapes, read as a continuum.
This is a count of rows. The notes on uniseriate and biseriate already say to move to a counted-arrangement expression rather than add one class per number.

label: glandular-apiculate
definition: A pointed quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's ending in a short, abrupt point tipped with a gland.
reason: No term exists. PATO has apiculate only as a synonym of the attribute sharpness. It is a sibling of FLOPO spine-tipped and applies to leaflets, sepals and teeth.
Most examples are 'accrescent' (growing larger after flowering). 'Increasing in diam.' along a tube is a gradient, not accrescence, and should not use this rule.
This is a ratio of two dimensions of one part, which the pattern already covers.
A part that does not persist is shed. In PATO's definition the quality belongs to the plant doing the shedding, while floras put it on the part that is shed, the same reading used for marcescent.
Tuberiform means shaped and thickened like a tuber, which is FLOPO tuberous.
A part 'with farina' is farinose, which the previous review mapped to mealy. The farina's colour and where it sits (abaxial side) are separate statements.

target: part of the bearer (docs/annotation-context-patterns.md slot 1): wing of the named organ + width (PATO_0000921)
reason: This is a measurement of the wing, a part of the seed or stem, not a new quality.
PATO discoid has the exact synonyms disc-shaped and disk-shaped.

label: doubly crenate
definition: A scalloped quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's margin bearing rounded teeth that are themselves crenate.
reason: This is a standard margin type. Mapping it to plain scalloped (crenate) would lose the second order of teeth, and it parallels the FLOPO bipinnate class.
This negates the existing FLOPO value ribbed.
'Ridges/keels without points' and 'pointless scales' say that the bearer has no point.

target: new: two values joined without a connector (both hold; not a continuum): spheroid (PATO_0001865) + flattened (PATO_0002254)
reason: This is a nearly round shape that is flattened, both at once. Unlike depressed-globose (oblate), 'compressed' usually means flattened from the sides, so oblate does not fit.
PATO blade-like has the synonyms sword-shaped and ensiform. A dagger shape is the same narrow, flat, sharp-pointed blade.
